name: Haskeri

anatomy.part: beak tip, top of the head

myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up so fast that Tavo the Gale came down the cold air to see what the noise was, and he laughed, and the wind tore through the gull-roost on the cliffs. One gull, grey as wet slate, was thrown too low over the Leeward. It had the names of the drowned in its beak, as gulls do, so that families could hear them said. Tavo spread its wings and would not let them fold. The gull went south and never came back. Hesk keeps count of the names, and she says they are still being carried. Look south on a clear night, low over the water, for two faint stars at the tips of the wings. When they shine, news is coming from the drowned. When they dim, someone on the islands should go and ask Kael, the Netter, who has cast for fallen stars all his life and has never caught one.
verse:
Two lamps on the wing,
look south where the tips hang low:
names come home, slow, cold.
